provenance.source: T-CAD repository results/ (last complete run; snake_case names, see snakeToCamelNameMap.json)
provenance.simulator: Synthetic PyGame/NumPy multi-vehicle simulator; 2-D ray-cast LiDAR; bounded synthetic message-level contradictions
provenance.ciMethod: 95% scenario-level bootstrap; seeds_better over 5 seed groups
provenance.hardware: Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0 · ARM64 · ARMv8 (64-bit) Family 8 Model 1 Revision 201 · 12 cores · 31.6 GB · Python 3.12.10
provenance.notComparableTo: Zhang et al. (2024) 91.5% detection / ~3% FPR — different data, attacks and metric denominators

descriptions.A0: Original CAD-inspired baseline (binary conflict area: occupancy + spoof + remove checks)
descriptions.A1: CAD + calibrated observations (conflicts weighted by calibrated likelihoods; pairwise)
descriptions.A2: CAD + Bayesian corroboration (leave-one-agent-out fused posterior, tempered)
descriptions.A3: CAD + HMM = CAD-HMM (per-source forward filters; pairwise; no cross-source fusion)
descriptions.A4: CAD + Bayesian corroboration + HMM (leave-one-out temporal fused filter)
descriptions.A5: Full T-CAD, interpretable rule (strong CAD alert OR A4 alert; abstain without corroboration)
descriptions.A5-LR: Full T-CAD, L2-regularised logistic-regression decision layer (+ strong CAD override)

calibrationParams.source: research-data/measured/demoCContradictory/model_artifacts.json (observation model used for the stored run)

researchQuestions.question: 1. Does CAD-HMM improve anomaly detection over CAD?
researchQuestions.answer: A3 vs A0: AUROC 0.911 -> 0.862, difference -0.049 [95% CI -0.068, -0.030], 45 test scenarios: deterioration; better in 0/5 seeds. At frozen thresholds: TPR TPR 0.521 -> 0.325, difference -0.196 [95% CI -0.243, -0.144], 45 test scenarios: deterioration; better in 0/5 seeds; FPR FPR 0.048 -> 0.052, difference 0.004 [95% CI -0.004, 0.011], 45 test scenarios: INCONCLUSIVE (95% CI includes 0); better in 4/5 seeds.

researchQuestions.question: 2. Does Bayesian corroboration improve detection independently of the HMM?
researchQuestions.answer: A2 vs A0: AUROC 0.911 -> 0.865, difference -0.046 [95% CI -0.076, -0.019], 45 test scenarios: deterioration; better in 0/5 seeds. Isolating fusion from calibration (A2 vs A1): AUROC 0.832 -> 0.865, difference 0.033 [95% CI 0.023, 0.043], 45 test scenarios: improvement; better in 5/5 seeds.
researchQuestions.evidence: results/model_comparisons.csv; paired bootstrap on test rows
researchQuestions.status: MIXED (better than calibrated-only CAD, worse than CAD)

researchQuestions.question: 3. Does combining Bayesian corroboration with HMM inference give an additional benefit?
researchQuestions.answer: A4 vs A2 (adding the HMM to fusion): AUROC 0.865 -> 0.913, difference 0.048 [95% CI 0.033, 0.067], 45 test scenarios: improvement; better in 5/5 seeds. A4 vs A3 (adding fusion to the HMM): AUROC 0.862 -> 0.913, difference 0.051 [95% CI 0.038, 0.065], 45 test scenarios: improvement; better in 5/5 seeds.

researchQuestions.question: 4. Under what noise conditions does temporal filtering help?
researchQuestions.answer: Adding the HMM to Bayesian corroboration (A4-A2) per LiDAR noise scale: noise x0.5: auroc 0.045 [0.017, 0.071] improves; noise x0.5: fpr 0.005 [-0.003, 0.015] inconclusive; noise x1.0: auroc 0.049 [0.017, 0.078] improves; noise x1.0: fpr -0.002 [-0.010, 0.007] inconclusive; noise x2.0: auroc 0.051 [0.022, 0.079] improves; noise x2.0: fpr -0.014 [-0.021, -0.009] improves; noise x4.0: auroc 0.051 [0.025, 0.085] improves; noise x4.0: fpr -0.036 [-0.045, -0.028] improves; noise x6.0: auroc 0.044 [0.020, 0.073] improves; noise x6.0: fpr -0.074 [-0.084, -0.061] improves. CAD-HMM vs CAD (A3-A0): x0.5: auroc -0.027 worsens; x0.5: fpr -0.000 inconclusive; x1.0: auroc -0.027 worsens; x1.0: fpr 0.000 inconclusive; x2.0: auroc -0.033 worsens; x2.0: fpr -0.000 inconclusive; x4.0: auroc -0.024 worsens; x4.0: fpr 0.019 worsens; x6.0: auroc -0.017 inconclusive; x6.0: fpr 0.037 worsens. Noise levels with a consistent improvement: 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 6.0.
researchQuestions.status: SUPPORTED when added to Bayesian fusion (all noise levels); NOT over CAD (A3-A0)

researchQuestions.question: 5. Does the HMM reduce false positives from transient benign errors?
researchQuestions.answer: Report-level FPR on reports from vehicles with an active benign fault: CAD A0 0.046 (lowest of the score-only configurations); A1 0.126 -> A3 0.086; A2 0.120 -> A4 0.092. Episode-level false-alarm rate on benign fault episodes: A0 0.260, A1 0.375, A2 0.368, A3 0.248, A4 0.255, A5 0.262, A5-LR 0.330. Paired FPR difference A4-A2 on these reports: -0.027 [-0.053, -0.018] (improves).
researchQuestions.status: SUPPORTED relative to A1/A2 (not below CAD)

researchQuestions.question: 6. Does the HMM delay detection of legitimate occupancy changes?
researchQuestions.answer: Legitimate occupancy changes: mean catch-up latency HMM 0.045 s vs instantaneous Bayesian 0.039 s (test split). Contradictory-report episodes: mean detection delay A0 0.334 s, A2 0.318 s, A3 0.430 s, A4 0.420 s, A5 0.392 s.
researchQuestions.status: SMALL EFFECT (HMM slower by < 1 frame; no CI)

researchQuestions.question: 7. What happens when independent corroborating observations are unavailable?
researchQuestions.answer: 12/3560 positive reports had a fabricated region not observed by any other vehicle. TPR observable vs unobservable: A0 0.523 vs 0.000, A2 0.350 vs 0.000, A4 0.532 vs 0.000, A5 0.512 vs 0.000. T-CAD abstains (insufficient evidence) on 0.000 of all report rows. R3 (A5 TPR by #CAVs): 2: 0.077, 3: 0.302, 4: 0.414, 6: 0.821. NOTE: the abstention rule (< 20 co-observed cells) never triggered in the test split, so the insufficient-evidence outcome is untested by this benchmark.

researchQuestions.question: 8. What happens when multiple sensors make correlated errors?
researchQuestions.answer: FPR on correlated-disturbance scenarios: independent/main/A2: 0.080 [0.070, 0.092]; independent/main/A4: 0.079 [0.073, 0.083]; independent/main/A5: 0.074 [0.069, 0.078]; shared/main/A2: 0.055 [0.049, 0.062]; shared/main/A4: 0.045 [0.037, 0.054]; shared/main/A5: 0.042 [0.034, 0.050]; independent/naive_independence/A2: 0.112 [0.101, 0.125]; independent/naive_independence/A4: 0.081 [0.077, 0.084]; independent/naive_independence/A5: 0.074 [0.071, 0.076]; shared/naive_independence/A2: 0.088 [0.077, 0.099]; shared/naive_independence/A4: 0.050 [0.039, 0.061]; shared/naive_independence/A5: 0.045 [0.036, 0.054]. Posterior NLL (tempered vs naive independence): independent: 0.0105 vs 0.0145; shared: 0.0107 vs 0.0151

researchQuestions.question: 9. How do results change as the number of vehicles increases?
researchQuestions.answer: A0 @ 2 CAVs: AUROC 0.769, TPR 0.175, FPR 0.001; A4 @ 2 CAVs: AUROC 0.803, TPR 0.090, FPR 0.000; A5 @ 2 CAVs: AUROC 0.804, TPR 0.077, FPR 0.000; A0 @ 3 CAVs: AUROC 0.888, TPR 0.337, FPR 0.017; A4 @ 3 CAVs: AUROC 0.889, TPR 0.321, FPR 0.009; A5 @ 3 CAVs: AUROC 0.890, TPR 0.302, FPR 0.009; A0 @ 4 CAVs: AUROC 0.849, TPR 0.393, FPR 0.035; A4 @ 4 CAVs: AUROC 0.862, TPR 0.423, FPR 0.035; A5 @ 4 CAVs: AUROC 0.857, TPR 0.414, FPR 0.035; A0 @ 6 CAVs: AUROC 0.939, TPR 0.748, FPR 0.085; A4 @ 6 CAVs: AUROC 0.939, TPR 0.826, FPR 0.116; A5 @ 6 CAVs: AUROC 0.937, TPR 0.821, FPR 0.115

researchQuestions.question: 10. How does T-CAD's runtime compare with the CAD-inspired baseline?
researchQuestions.answer: Model inference latency per ego vehicle per frame (test split, 10 parallel workers): A0 p50 17.1 / p95 28.3 ms, A1 p50 24.6 / p95 38.7 ms, A2 p50 26.1 / p95 40.7 ms, A3 p50 35.2 / p95 54.3 ms, A4 p50 40.9 / p95 62.4 ms, A5 p50 46.8 / p95 70.4 ms, A5-LR p50 59.3 / p95 88.6 ms. R10 sequential benchmark, p95 by #CAVs: A0@2.0: 3.6 ms; A5@2.0: 9.8 ms; A0@4.0: 11.3 ms; A5@4.0: 28.5 ms; A0@6.0: 20.2 ms; A5@6.0: 56.5 ms; A0@8.0: 27.9 ms; A5@8.0: 75.5 ms

researchQuestions.question: 11. Which modelling component contributes most to measured improvements?
researchQuestions.answer: Largest AUROC gain: logistic decision layer (A5-LR vs A4): 0.057 [0.037, 0.077]. All steps: A5-LR vs A4 0.057 (improves); A4 vs A2 0.048 (improves); A2 vs A1 0.033 (improves); A3 vs A1 0.030 (improves); A1 vs A0 -0.079 (worsens)

researchQuestions.question: 12. Which modelling component causes the largest regressions?
researchQuestions.answer: Consistent deteriorations: A1 vs A0 (calibrated likelihood weighting) auroc -0.079 [-0.111, -0.051]; A1 vs A0 (calibrated likelihood weighting) tpr -0.248 [-0.303, -0.191]; A5 vs A4 (rule-based decision layer) tpr -0.020 [-0.024, -0.014]

researchQuestions.question: 13. Are the posterior probabilities calibrated?
researchQuestions.answer: Occupancy posteriors on the test split (cells observed by >= 1 source): bayes_calibrated: ECE 0.0016, Brier 0.0036, NLL 0.0111; bayes_nominal: ECE 0.0077, Brier 0.0048, NLL 0.0181; bayes_naive: ECE 0.0032, Brier 0.0042, NLL 0.0156; hmm_calibrated: ECE 0.0059, Brier 0.0059, NLL 0.0338; single_ego: ECE 0.0015, Brier 0.0027, NLL 0.0079. Anomaly scores (A1-A4) are evidence areas, not probabilities; only A5-LR outputs a probability, whose calibration is not claimed (class-balanced training shifts it).

researchQuestions.question: 14. Are improvements robust across scenarios and random seeds?
researchQuestions.answer: Seeds/runs where each configuration beats A0 on AUROC: A1 0/5, A2 0/5, A3 0/5, A4 3/5, A5 3/5, A5-LR 5/5. Per-family HMM effects (figure 20): A3-A1 contradictory AUROC 0.002 [-0.012, 0.016]; A3-A1 correlated_errors FPR (lower=better) -0.018 [-0.030, -0.011]; A3-A1 missing_observations AUROC 0.043 [0.030, 0.056]; A3-A1 moving_object FPR (lower=better) 0.013 [-0.005, 0.030]; A3-A1 normal FPR (lower=better) -0.004 [-0.010, 0.004]; A3-A1 occlusion FPR (lower=better) 0.002 [0.001, 0.003]; A3-A1 persistent_fabrication AUROC -0.013 [-0.032, 0.003]; A3-A1 removal AUROC 0.089 [0.031, 0.149]; A3-A1 transient_noise FPR (lower=better) -0.010 [-0.017, -0.002]; A4-A2 contradictory AUROC 0.024 [0.007, 0.037]; A4-A2 correlated_errors FPR (lower=better) -0.009 [-0.014, -0.004]; A4-A2 missing_observations AUROC 0.032 [0.019, 0.043]; A4-A2 moving_object FPR (lower=better) 0.012 [-0.000, 0.020]; A4-A2 normal FPR (lower=better) -0.003 [-0.010, 0.004]; A4-A2 occlusion FPR (lower=better) -0.000 [-0.003, 0.003]; A4-A2 persistent_fabrication AUROC 0.035 [0.023, 0.046]; A4-A2 removal AUROC 0.104 [0.032, 0.185]; A4-A2 transient_noise FPR (lower=better) 0.002 [-0.006, 0.010]

researchQuestions.question: 15. What limitations prevent claims about real-world deployment?
researchQuestions.answer: 2D single-plane synthetic LiDAR; simple kinematics; synthetic, non-adaptive contradictory reports; scenario distribution designed by us; Python prototype timings on a desktop; no real V2X, no real sensor data. See docs/limitations.md.
